## Body

Budget the final message, including generated repair-command footers.

#208's request-line loop had a 2 KB check but appended every distinct release command in an unbounded footer and always kept the first line. Sixty requests to one address passed because the footer deduplicated to one command; ordinary requests to many addresses broke the cap. This was a normal-use C34 correctness/cost defect, not same-user hardening.

The final repair at 808d10d7fb9c2f6cd76ab07198791281b8974aca limits the footer to three complete commands plus its omitted count. The distinct-address regression checks the whole body; closure output is 131eb28ee538a63394b2ebb0b855606f2cb9298b.

When changing grouped notices, account for header, body, separators, footer and omission text together. Keep complete labels/commands rather than cutting through characters or shell words. Check a representative input that makes the footer grow independently of the body. A body-only cap or a single-address fixture proves less than a whole-message budget. Under C34, verify the requested fix; additional exhaustive fixtures and mutants are optional, not gates.
